## Overview

**In plain terms.** Among children whose phonetic-spelling score was observed to be zero before randomisation, did those offered the intervention become more likely to score above zero at t2? Random assignment would support a causal contrast for a pre-treatment subgroup whose eligibility and follow-up outcomes were observed for the original randomised cohort. This fitted subgroup is selected by archive inclusion, observed baseline eligibility and observed t2 outcome, so a causal reading requires that selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential off-floor outcomes. Extending the result to all 57 randomised children requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity; the subgroup estimand is also post-hoc.

LRPITT09 is an available-case, modified-ITT reanalysis of phonetic spelling (`spphon`) over the randomised t1 $\rightarrow$ t2 phase. At baseline, 42/54 children (about 78%) scored zero; at t2, 34/53 observed scores (about 64%) were zero. One baseline-floor child lacks a t2 score, leaving 41 children eligible for the transition analysis (24 intervention, 17 control).

_Post-hoc floored-outcome estimand — exploratory headline._ The floor rule and its 40% threshold were adopted after inspecting these outcome distributions and earlier model results. It is therefore **post-hoc and data-adaptive**, not pre-registered or prospectively specified. Applying the mechanical gate without arm labels reduces treatment-effect-driven selection, but does not change that evidential status. Under this rule the model:

- drops the degenerate own baseline and uses an **age-only** predictor;
- reports $\Pr(\text{post} > 0 \mid \text{observed pre} = 0)$ among the **observed baseline-floor subgroup** as the exploratory headline. Defining a subgroup by a fully observed pre-randomisation score would not itself undo randomisation, but this subgroup also requires archive inclusion, observed eligibility and observed t2 outcome. Its causal reading therefore requires that those selection steps did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential off-floor outcomes; and
- retains two flagged, **detection-limited secondaries**, read only alongside the per-arm mover counts: the graded Beta-Binomial $\tau$ over all outcome-available children, and the **graded contrast among off-floor children** ($\text{post} > 0$). The latter is an untruncated proxy for $\mathrm{E}[\text{post} \mid \text{post} > 0]$ and conditions on a post-randomisation event, so it is not a randomised causal effect.

_Analysis population and eligibility._ The published trial randomised 57 children (29 intervention, 28 wait-list), whereas the archived repository dataset contains 54 (28 intervention, 26 wait-list); phonetic spelling is observed at t2 for 53. This is therefore not a full-randomised-cohort ITT analysis. Each fit writes `baseline_floor_eligibility.csv` and records the same arm-specific counts in `config.json`; extending the subgroup result to all 57 requires explicit assumptions or sensitivity analyses for unavailable participants, unknown eligibility and missing outcomes.

_Identification and sign convention._ Under the locked causal DAG, $G$ is a randomised root, so the offer contrast in the original full randomised cohort requires the **empty adjustment set**. A fully observed subgroup defined by pre-randomisation floor status would likewise require no baseline-covariate adjustment. This fit instead conditions on archive inclusion, observed eligibility and observed outcome; a causal reading of $\tau$ requires that this selection did not induce an association between assigned arm and potential off-floor outcomes, while extension to all 57 requires further missing-data assumptions and sensitivity. Linear age is a precision term only. **Sign convention:** $G = 1$ is the intervention arm, so a **positive** $\tau$ means the intervention arm has the higher modelled probability of coming off the floor.

## Model

Exploratory headline (binary off-floor transition among children with observed $P_{\text{pre}}=0$), with $\eta_i = \alpha + \tau\,G_i + \gamma_A\,A_{\text{std},i}$:

$$
[\,P_{\text{post},i} > 0\,] \sim \text{Bernoulli}\big(\sigma(\eta_i)\big).
$$

SECONDARY (graded, detection-limited): the *same* age-only $\eta_i$ with a
Beta-Binomial likelihood on the count, $P_{\text{post},i} \sim \text{BetaBinomial}(N, \mu_i\kappa, (1-\mu_i)\kappa)$, $N = 92$.
